subject.title: [Feature]: First-class user identity for shared gateways (presence, viewers, attribution, profiles)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a first-class, gateway-attested optional user-identity model for shared trusted-proxy gateways, and what minimum privacy and persistence contract should the first implementation stage guarantee?
rationale: The requested feature introduces new durable user records, exposed presence/viewer information, transcript attribution, RPC/CLI/UI surface, and future authorization scope semantics; these are product and security-boundary choices rather than a mechanically determined bug fix.

options.title: Sponsor a staged core design
options.body: Approve a narrowly scoped first stage for trusted-proxy identity threading and additive presence attribution, with profiles and viewer UI specified in follow-up design work.

options.title: Limit the scope to attribution
options.body: Adopt only connection-derived prompt attribution and defer durable profiles, viewing presence, and user-management APIs until a separate product decision.

options.title: Route identity to an extension boundary
options.body: Keep core gateway identity transport minimal and require profile management or collaboration UI to be implemented through a plugin once the needed generic seams are defined.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a staged core design
recommendation.body: Approve a narrowly scoped first stage for trusted-proxy identity threading and additive presence attribution, with profiles and viewer UI specified in follow-up design work.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue identifies @steipete as the requester for the shared-team-instance program and proposes an implementation train requiring product sponsorship.
